arxiv-1804-06044.title: A Scalable Permission Management System With Support for Conditional and Customized Attributes
arxiv-1804-06044.creator: Baiyu Liu, Abhinav Palia, Shan-Ho Yang
arxiv-1804-06044.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Baiyu Liu, Abhinav Palia, Shan-Ho Yang. Along with the classical problem of managing multiple identities, actions, devices, APIs etc. in different businesses, there has been an escalating need for having the capability of flexible attribute based access control (ABAC) mechanisms. In order to fill this gap, several variations of ABAC model have been proposed such as Amazon’s AWS IAM , which uses JSON as their underlying storage data structure and adds policies/constraints as fields over the regular ABAC.

arxiv-2111-11842.title: A short noncomplex proof for the solution set of homogeneous second order linear differential equations with constant coefficients
arxiv-2111-11842.creator: Patrik Lundström
arxiv-2111-11842.description: Abstract . We provide a short proof, not utilizing complex numbers, for the solution set of homogeneous second order linear differential equations with constant coefficients. We argue that the solution set of second order linear differential equations with constant coefficients should be presented using hyperbolic functions in the distinct real root case: Theorem. Let a,b\in\mathbb{R} .

arxiv-2112-02526.title: On the Numerical Approximation of the Karhunen-Loève Expansion for Random Fields with Random Discrete Data
arxiv-2112-02526.creator: Michael Griebel, Guanglian Li, Christian Rieger
arxiv-2112-02526.description: Abstract Many physical and mathematical models involve random fields in their input data. Examples are ordinary differential equations, partial differential equations and integro–differential equations with uncertainties in the coefficient functions described by random fields. They also play a dominant role in problems in machine learning.

arxiv-2206-04010.title: Strongly contracting axes for fully irreducible automorphisms of Generalized Baumslag-Solitar groups
arxiv-2206-04010.creator: Chloé Papin
arxiv-2206-04010.description: Abstract Similarly to the action of O ​ u ​ t ​ ( F N ) Out(F_{N}) on Outer Space, the outer automorphism group of a Generalized Baumslag Solitar group acts on a deformation space endowed with the Lipschitz metric and the action of any fully irreducible automorphism with a train track representative is hyperbolic.

arxiv-2210-07366.title: A Generalization of Markov Numbers
arxiv-2210-07366.creator: Esther Banaian, Archan Sen
arxiv-2210-07366.description: Abstract We explore a generalization of the Markov numbers that is motivated by a specific generalized cluster algebra arising from an orbifold, in the sense of Chekhov and Shapiro. We give an explicit algorithm for computing these generalized Markov numbers and exhibit several patterns analogous to those that appear within the ordinary Markov numbers.

arxiv-2212-03214.title: Generalized Belief Propagation Algorithms for Decoding of Surface Codes
arxiv-2212-03214.creator: Josias Old, Manuel Rispler
arxiv-2212-03214.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Josias Old, Manuel Rispler. Belief propagation (BP) is well-known as a low complexity decoding algorithm with a strong performance for important classes of quantum error correcting codes, e.g. notably for the quantum low-density parity check (LDPC) code class of random expander codes. However, it is also well-known that the performance of BP breaks down when facing topological codes such as the surface code, where naive BP fails entirely to reach a below-threshold regime, i.e. the regime where error correction becomes useful.

arxiv-2303-08568.title: Generating contingency tables with fixed marginal probabilities and dependence structures described by loglinear models
arxiv-2303-08568.creator: Ceejay Hammond, Peter G.M. van der Heijden, Paul A. Smith
arxiv-2303-08568.description: Abstract We present a method to generate contingency tables that follow loglinear models with prescribed marginal probabilities and dependence structures. We make use of (loglinear) Poisson regression, where the dependence structures, described using odds ratios, are implemented using an offset term.

arxiv-2306-15361.title: Observation of Two-Dimensional Acoustic Bound States in the Continuum
arxiv-2306-15361.creator: Marc Martí-Sabaté, Junfei Li, Bahram Djafari-Rouhani, Steven A. Cummer, Dani Torrent
arxiv-2306-15361.description: Abstract The design of devices based on acoustic or optical fields requires the fabrication of cavities and structures capable of efficiently trapping these waves. A special type of cavity can be designed to support resonances with a theoretically infinite quality factor, named bound states in the continuum or BICs.

arxiv-2312-16086.title: Notes on Retroactive Interference Model of Forgetting
arxiv-2312-16086.creator: Mikhail Katkov
arxiv-2312-16086.description: Abstract We present analytical derivation of the minimal and maximal number of items retained in recently introduced Retroactive Interference Model of Forgetting. Also we computed the probability that two items presented at different times are retained in the memory at a later time analytically.

arxiv-2407-05274.title: Weyl’s Law for compact rank one symmetric spaces
arxiv-2407-05274.creator: Sai Sriharsha Indukuri, Ritwik Mukherjee
arxiv-2407-05274.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sai Sriharsha Indukuri, Ritwik Mukherjee. Weyl’s law is a fundamental result governing the asymptotic behaviour of the eigenvalues of the Laplacian. It states that for a compact d d dimensional manifold M M (without boundary), the eigenvalue counting function N M ​ ( λ ) N_{M}(\lambda) has the following asymptotic growth N M ​ ( λ ) = Vol ​ ( M ) ​ ( ω d ( 2 ​ π ) d ) ​ λ d + O ⁡ ( λ d −

arxiv-2509-17432.title: In vivo and predictive interplay evaluation methodology for lung and esophageal cancer patients treated in free breathing with IMPT
arxiv-2509-17432.creator: Giorgio Cartechini, Esther Kneepkens, Gloria Vilches-Freixas, Indra Lubken, Marije Velders, Sebastiaan Nijsten, Mirko Unipan, Ilaria Rinaldi
arxiv-2509-17432.description: Abstract Purpose: Pencil beam scanning proton therapy is sensitive to respiratory motion, leading to potential dose inhomogeneities due to interplay effects. We developed and validated a predictive framework to assess interplay and motion robustness in lung and esophageal cancer patients treated under free-breathing conditions.

arxiv-2510-05613.title: PointNSP : Autoregressive 3D Point Cloud Generation with Next-Scale Level-of-Detail Prediction
arxiv-2510-05613.creator: Ziqiao Meng Qichao Wang Zhiyang Dou Zixing Song Zhipeng Zhou, Irwin King Peilin Zhao
arxiv-2510-05613.description: Abstract Autoregressive point cloud generation has long lagged behind diffusion-based approaches in quality. The performance gap stems from the fact that autoregressive models impose an artificial ordering on inherently unordered point sets, forcing shape generation to proceed as a sequence of local predictions.

arxiv-2602-02669.title: Structure and Evolution of Multi-Cluster within Galactic Disc: Gaia DR3 Insights into Eight Open Clusters
arxiv-2602-02669.creator: A. Ahmed 1,*, W. H. Elsanhoury 2, D. C. Çınar 3, A. A. Haroon 4,5, M. S. Alenazi 2 and E. A. Elkholy 2,5
arxiv-2602-02669.description: Abstract In this study, we present a comprehensive analysis of the structural, astrophysical, and dynamical properties of eight open clusters: NGC 559, NGC 1817, NGC 2141, NGC 7245, Ruprecht 15, Ruprecht 137, Ruprecht 142, and Ruprecht 169, utilizing the precise astrometric and photometric data from G ​ a ​ i ​ a Gaia Data Release 3.

plos-pone-0004515.title: Changes in Weight, Waist Circumference and Compensatory Responses with Different Doses of Exercise among Sedentary, Overweight Postmenopausal Women
plos-pone-0004515.creator: Timothy S. Church, Corby K. Martin, Angela M. Thompson et al.
plos-pone-0004515.description: PLOS ONE research article. It has been suggested that exercise training results in compensatory mechanisms that attenuate weight loss. However, this has only been examined with large doses of exercise. The goal of this analysis was to examine actual weight loss compared to predicted weight loss (compensati

plos-pone-0009761.title: T Cell Specific Adapter Protein (TSAd) Interacts with Tec Kinase ITK to Promote CXCL12 Induced Migration of Human and Murine T Cells
plos-pone-0009761.creator: Tone Berge, Vibeke Sundvold-Gjerstad, Stine Granum et al.
plos-pone-0009761.description: PLOS ONE research article. T Cell Specific Adapter Protein (TSAd) Interacts with Tec Kinase ITK to Promote CXCL12 Induced Migration of Human and Murine T Cells

pmc-10565953.title: Exploring relationships between pre-service teachers’ self-efficacy for writing and instruction provided in simulated elementary writing conferences
pmc-10565953.creator: Amy Gillespie Rouse, Murphy K. Young, Diane Gifford
pmc-10565953.description: Practice-based opportunities, like teaching simulations, are becoming more prevalent in teacher preparation programs. We sought to examine the instructional moves of 5 pre-service teachers during a simulated elementary writing conference using Mursion technology, a mixed-reality simulation (MRS) that emulates a classroom environment with student avatars. We examined both participants’ self-efficacy and their instructional moves during MRS writing conferences.

pmc-10605833.title: Breast and Formula Milk and Early Puberty Onset
pmc-10605833.creator: Valeria Calcaterra, Hellas Cena, Francesca Sottotetti, Virginia Rossi, Federica Loperfido, Gianvincenzo Zuccotti
pmc-10605833.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Nutrients have an enormous impact on many hormonal systems and aspects of health, and nutrition status is a crucial regulator of growth and pubertal development in children and adolescents. In this narrative review, we explore the connection between these feeding methods and the timing of puberty to provide a clearer understanding of how infant nutrition might contribute to the early development of puberty.

pmc-11422631.title: Molecular typing methods to characterize Brucella spp. from animals: A review
pmc-11422631.creator: Aida Daugaliyeva, Saule Daugaliyeva, Nazerke Kydyr, Simone Peletto
pmc-11422631.description: Brucellosis is an infectious disease of animals that can infect humans. The disease causes significant economic losses and threatens human health. A timely and accurate disease diagnosis plays a vital role in the identification of brucellosis. In addition to traditional diagnostic methods, molecular methods allow diagnosis and typing of the causative agent of brucellosis.

pmc-11545499.title: Regulatory Mechanism of Protein Crotonylation and Its Relationship with Cancer
pmc-11545499.creator: Siyi Yang, Xinyi Fan, Wei Yu, Aurelio Lorico
pmc-11545499.description: Crotonylation is a recently discovered protein acyl modification that shares many enzymes with acetylation. However, it possesses a distinct regulatory mechanism and biological function due to its unique crotonyl structure. Since the discovery of crotonylation in 2011, numerous crotonylation sites have been identified in both histones and other proteins.

pmc-11714420.title: Can accelerometry identify/monitor neuropsychiatric symptoms correlated with motor activity in persons living with dementia? Results from a diagnostic test accuracy systematic review
pmc-11714420.creator: Elena Guseva, Andrea Iaboni, Krista L Lanctôt, Nathan Herrmann, Zahinoor Ismail, Amer M Burhan, Genevieve Gore, Dallas Seitz, Sanjeev Kumar, Marie‐Andrée Bruneau, Andrew Lim, Machelle Wilchesky
pmc-11714420.description: BackgroundWearable sensor technology shows promise for neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPS) identification/monitoring in persons living with dementia (PLWD). Accelerometry measures acceleration of body segments and physical activity. This study explores the diagnostic test accuracy (DTA) of accelerometry to identify the following 6 NPS associated with motor activity: aberrant motor behavior (AMB), aggression, agitation, anxiety, apathy, and wandering.

pmc-12395846.title: A systematic analysis assessing epidemiological characteristics and surgical outcomes of posterolateral tibial plateau fractures
pmc-12395846.creator: Qinglin Qiu, Zeyu Zhang, Zhongpei Lin, Xiaoyue Wen, Shouwen Su, Bo He
pmc-12395846.description: ObjectiveTo analyze the Schatzker classification and related epidemiological situation of posterolateral tibial plateau fractures (PTPFs), and analyze the curative effect of different surgical approaches and internal fixation methods according to the subtype of PTPFs, to provide a strategic basis for clinicians to treat posterolateral plateau fractures.

pmc-12429383.title: Role of RhoGEFs or RhoGAPs in Pyk2-Mediated RhoA Activation in Depolarization-Induced Contraction of Rat Caudal Arterial Smooth Muscle
pmc-12429383.creator: Kazuki Aida, Mitsuo Mita, Reiko Ishii-Nozawa, Ida Daniela Perrotta
pmc-12429383.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). It has previously been reported that the RhoA/Rho-associated kinase (ROCK) pathway is involved in depolarization-induced contraction triggered by high [K+] stimulation in rat caudal arterial smooth muscle. Furthermore, we reported that activation of the upstream Ca2+-dependent proline-rich tyrosine kinase 2 (Pyk2) leads to phosphorylation of myosin targeting subunit of myosin light chain phosphatase (MYPT1) and 20 kDa myosin light chain (LC20).

pmc-12727854.title: Analysis of variations in cell envelope subproteome and cell length in Acinetobacter baumannii ATCC 19606T populations by effect of temperature and desiccation
pmc-12727854.creator: Maite Orruño, Zaloa Bravo, Iciar Martinez, Inés Arana
pmc-12727854.description: Acinetobacter baumannii, a pathogen for humans and animals, possesses a tremendous potential to survive under hostile conditions. We studied the effect of temperature, nutrient deprivation, and desiccation on the survival of A. baumannii ATCC 19606T by monitoring variations in cellular counts and in cell length and analyzing cell envelope subproteome during the survival process.

pmc-13043908.title: Validation of the Updated Digital Health Literacy Instrument and Development of a Short Form: Online Survey Study of the General Population
pmc-13043908.creator: Rosalie van der Vaart, Inge Tuitert, Job van 't Veer, Constance Drossaert
pmc-13043908.description: BackgroundThe digital health literacy instrument (DHLI) was developed in 2017 to measure individuals’ ability to access, understand, evaluate, and apply online health information. Since that time, digital health has shifted from desktop-based internet use to mobile devices, and there has been a rapidly expanding range of health apps.

pmc-13363103.title: Effects of Sacubitril/Valsartan versus Irbesartan on Urine Tubular Biomarkers in Chronic Kidney Disease: Findings from the UK HARP-III Trial
pmc-13363103.creator: Michelle A. Goonasekera, Greco B. Malijan, Rebecca J. Sardell, Natalie Staplin, Benjamin S. Storey, Daniel Chapman, Michael Hill, Stewart Moffat, Abdulrahman Al-Mohammad, Doreen Zhu, Nigel J. Brunskill, John J.V. McMurray, Maarten W. Taal, William G. Herrington, Martin J. Landray, Colin Baigent, Ric
pmc-13363103.description: IntroductionSacubitril/valsartan shows benefits in heart failure and may have kidney protective effects. Its impact on kidney tubular health in chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains unclear. We evaluated the effects of sacubitril/valsartan on urinary markers of tubular dysfunction and injury in UK Heart and Renal Protection-III (HARP III, ISRCTN:11958993).

pmc-13651769.title: Ultrasensitive SERS detection via hydrodynamic focusing coupled with electric field induced migration
pmc-13651769.creator: Monika Poonia, Zachary D. Schultz
pmc-13651769.description: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) offers a powerful platform for ultrasensitive molecular detection, yet its performance is often limited by inefficient analyte transport to plasmonic hotspots. In this work, we present a hybrid microfluidic-SERS detection platform that integrates hydrodynamic focusing and electric field-induced migration to overcome diffusion limitations and enhance molecular delivery to the sensing interface.

uslaw-usc-t20-s7245.title: 20 U.S.C. § 7245 — Family engagement in Indian schools
uslaw-usc-t20-s7245.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t20-s7245.description: United States Code, Title 20 (Education); Chapter 70 (Strengthening And Improvement Of Elementary And Secondary Schools); Subchapter IV (21St Century Schools); Part E (Family Engagement In Education Programs). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary of the Interior, in consultation with the Secretary of Education, shall establish, or enter into contracts and cooperative agreements with, local tribes, tribal organizations, or Indian nonprofit.
